text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: customer=Atlas-MLHub cluster=dedicated-eu-west-2-42 elevated 5xx rate > 8% (gateway 502/504 + model 5xx)

maya: oncall here, looking

sam: seeing same, dashboards show latency spike on `gateway-proxy` and queue length on `infer-worker` for tenant atlas-mlhub up 6x in last 10m

cheng: logs show a lot of `ERROR: model shard OOM` and request rejections from the allocator, plus repeated reconnects from runner-3

ryan: probably noisy neighbor on that GPU pool. tenant atlas-other had a burst earlier. Any throttle rules applied?

maya: checked rate limits — nothing unusual. Autoscaler didn't add nodes; pool cpu/gpu util at 98% and pod eviction count increased. Looks like capacity exhaustion rather than pure rate.

katie: tagging runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/runbooks/dedicated-capacity#noisy-neighbor

maya: action plan: 1) divert new atlas-mlhub requests to fallback pool (if capacity) 2) throttle heavy tenants on same pool 3) provision burst nodes 4) contact customer (atlas-support) with ETA.

sam: running quick traffic shift: `rbacctl route set --from tenant=atlas-mlhub --to pool=dedicated-burst-1 --weight=100 --dry-run` then apply.

sam: applied `rbacctl route set --from tenant=atlas-mlhub --to pool=dedicated-burst-1 --weight=100` — responses routing now show ~75% diverted, gateway errors dropping to ~3%

incident-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation step applied by sam, tag=traffic-shift, incident_id=INC-20260401-42

maya: good. next, throttle noisy neighbor: identifying top consumers on pool. `kqc top-tenants --pool=eu-west-2-42 --window=5m` shows atlas-other at 62% of tokens.

cheng: applying soft throttle on atlas-other: `quotactl update atlas-other --max-tokens-per-min 80000 --burst 10000`

cheng: throttle applied. atlas-other client reports some latency but error rate for atlas-mlhub trending down to 1.2%

ryan: provisioning burst nodes with infra: `allocctl request --pool eu-west-2-42 --gpus 2 --type p4d-burst` ETA ~8m. ops-bot: will that require infra-oncall?

ops-bot: alloc request accepted, job 0x7a1 queued on infra. Provisioning ETA 7m.

maya: can someone confirm model fallback is enabled for atlas-mlhub? fallback to `redwood-small-v2` if primary fails.

sam: fallback already in policy but weight is 0. Increasing fallback weight to 25% while pool recovers. `policyctl set atlas-mlhub fallback_weight=25`

sam: fallback applied. Observability: token cost down, p95 latency dropping from 2.4s to 1.1s for atlas-mlhub requests. 5xxs at 0.9% now.

atlas-support: thanks team — customers seeing degraded, but accepted routing to fallback as temporary. Please share ETA.

maya: provisioning completed, new nodes joined pool. We should remove aggressive fallback and throttle in stages.

cheng: rolling back throttle: `quotactl update atlas-other --max-tokens-per-min 300000 --burst 50000`

sam: reducing fallback weight to 5% and shifting atlas-mlhub back to main pool by 80%: `rbacctl route set --from tenant=atlas-mlhub --to pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-42 --weight=80`

maya: summary for handoff to next oncall (ryan): incident: INC-20260401-42. Customer: Atlas-MLHub. Impact: elevated 5xx/504 due to capacity exhaustion / noisy neighbor on dedicated pool eu-west-2-42. Actions taken: traffic diverted to burst pool, soft-throttled noisy tenant (atlas-other), provisioned burst nodes, increased fallback to smaller model, restored normal routing. Current status: stable, 5xx < 1%, latency near baseline.

ryan: taking over oncall. Steps to follow in morning: 1) run detailed heap/kv cache check on infer-workers 2) validate autoscaler config for pool (scale thresholds) 3) follow up with capacity team on preemptive burst policy 4) draft customer-facing note with kpis and action items.

maya: adding postmortem owners: sam + cheng. Please collect timeline and logs (s3://redwood-logs/incidents/INC-20260401-42) and include reproduce steps if any.

incident-bot: Incident status: acknowledged -> mitigated by sam at 1840001500, status=monitoring

maya: leaving a few outstanding tasks: customer comm, postmortem, update runbook with a checklist for auto-burst thresholds. I'll create follow-up ticket.
